# Home Environment Manager v0.6.0b67 - recovery and AQI only

## Recovery scope

This is a conservative recovery release following a report that Beta66 made Home Assistant unresponsive. It is based on the exact Beta65 release (96936bf590774355f83eeaaebe120f8153af2c41), not on an unverified patch to Beta66.

- Restores the pre-Beta66 native controller, supply controller, sleep/cooldown, existing window interlocks, startup logic and card interaction implementation. CI verifies these source files are byte-for-byte unchanged from Beta65.
- The new Beta66 per-device window-stop switch/60-second recovery policy and Beta66 dashboard interaction additions are temporarily withdrawn. Saved user options, controller identities, manual latches and physical settings are not deleted. The older window safety checks still apply; this recovery is not a new implementation of the Beta66 feature.
- Keeps Beta65 translations, collapsible calibration, device summaries, optional-warning neutrality and informational lux support.
- No SAT integration, new PID tuning, new calibration algorithm or new device control features.

The precise cause of the reported freeze has not been confirmed from installation logs. This rollback removes the Beta66 changes from the active path; it is not a claim of verified resolution on the user's hardware.

## AQI configuration reliably exists during startup

AQI scale and custom-limit configuration entities are now registered from saved outdoor source selections and the entity registry, even before the provider has produced its first live state. Their existing unique IDs are preserved, and unknown/unavailable physical sensor data no longer prevents editing configuration.

A source whose AQI metadata arrives late is registered once using listeners scoped to configured outdoor sensor IDs. No polling loop, full HA state scan, registry enumeration, settings reload or physical service call is added by those listeners. Ordinary numeric changes do not republish unchanged configuration controls.

## WAQI is automatically recognized

A source whose actual registered integration platform is `waqi` is interpreted as US EPA AQI by default. This is based on provider identity, not a guessed value, unit, city, friendly name, or arbitrary attribute. It applies only to AQ index sources, not WAQI pollutant-concentration sensors.

- No manual scale entry is necessary for a recognized WAQI source without an explicit override.
- Existing explicit US EPA, EEA category or custom settings take priority.
- `Automatic (provider)` restores provider detection; `Unknown - no comparison` explicitly disables interpretation.
- Other unrecognized providers remain unconfigured rather than being assumed safe.
- The scale selector exposes the effective scale and its provenance in attributes. Names use the station's friendly name plus a localized AQI scale/custom limit label in all 38 supported languages.
- The existing options page is reachable: Home Environment Manager options -> Outside data -> Outside / AQI. It works with offline registered sources and supports an explicit manual override.

HA's WAQI documentation describes the US EPA category boundaries: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/waqi/

## Validation

The release checks real source functions and configuration classes under simulated HA registry/entity interfaces: source absent at startup, renamed sources, late metadata, unchanged unique IDs, duplicate-event prevention, provider provenance, manual override persistence, custom thresholds, unknown scales, the actual outdoor classification pipeline, all 38 localized selectors and 10,000 relevant plus 10,000 unrelated state events. Unbounded state/registry enumeration and hardware services fail the tests.

Previous Beta61-65 supply, cold-start, sleep/cooldown, PID-race, warning/lux and actual Chromium card regressions remain in the suite. The source is also checked for exact recovery-baseline identity, Python/JavaScript syntax, JSON validity and canonical ZIP layout. These are not full Home Assistant installation or physical appliance tests.

## Upgrade

Upgrade/redownload the existing Home Environment Manager repository in HACS to **v0.6.0b67**, restart Home Assistant and fully reload the dashboard browser tab so the old Beta66 JavaScript is no longer running. Do not reinstall Beta66.

If the integration code was quarantined for recovery, HACS redownload restores the canonical `custom_components/environment_manager` folder; keep the existing configuration entry and settings. Do not restore the quarantined Beta66 source over the new release. The integration domain remains `environment_manager` and no duplicate integration should be added.
